title: Al-Baqi, the Everlasting
tomorrow: Dadi wants to give it all away now. should she wait?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Badi', the Originator: He says to a thing only, Be, and it is. The line was without precedent. And a riddle was left on the table: a sheep given away, and somehow it remains.

Moving sales run on strange math. The couch goes for almost nothing, the lamp for free, and the thing that cost the most leaves first. Here is a stranger sum, from a hadith. A sheep was slaughtered in the Prophet's household, peace be upon him, and the meat was given away. He asked what was left. Aisha said only the shoulder remained. And he answered: all of it remains, except its shoulder. The part they kept was the part that was gone.
screen: `MOVING-SALE MATH.` → `ONLY THE SHOULDER REMAINS.` → `ALL OF IT REMAINS, EXCEPT…`

segments.voice: To solve it, start with the Name. Al-Baqi, the Everlasting, the One who remains. The Qur'an puts it plainly in Surah al-Qasas: "Everything will perish save His countenance." Phones, houses, mountains, the people we love. Everything has an ending except Him. Now the second key, from Surah an-Nahl, in Pickthall's words: "That which ye have wasteth away, and that which Allah hath remaineth." Two piles. What you hold runs out: the shoulder gets eaten, the dishes chip, the couch sags. What is with Allah stays, because He stays. So the riddle opens. Meat given as sadaqa, charity, has moved from the first pile to the second. It's with the One who remains, so it remains. The shoulder they kept for dinner was simply dinner. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: in that hadith, the kitchen math runs backward. What leaves your hands is what you keep. None of this makes owning things wrong; the family still ate the shoulder. It changes the grip. If He remains, then the things that pass can be held loosely, enjoyed, and let go.
screen: `EVERYTHING PERISHES BUT HIM.` · `WHAT YE HAVE WASTETH AWAY.` · `GIVEN = WITH THE ONE WHO STAYS.` · `HOLD WHAT PASSES LOOSELY.` · then, large: `HE REMAINS.`

segments.voice: Put something small that you like in your open palm: a ring, a key, a pen. Rest your hand on your knee, palm up, fingers relaxed, and don't close them around it for the whole sit. Let it be held without being gripped.
Al-Baqi. The Everlasting, who remains when everything else has passed.
Keep this close: he remains, and so does whatever you've given into his hands. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims give sadaqa, voluntary charity, alongside the required zakat; the hadith of the sheep is often told to explain why what is given is what lasts.

match.prompt: solve the riddle — tap the pairs.

myth: Al-Baqi just means Allah lasts longer than other things
it's not a longer lifespan: everything will perish save His countenance.
in the hadith, the part that 'remains' is the part given away
all of it remains, except its shoulder: the shoulder was the part they kept.

fork.setup: your little brother's sandcastle just washed away and he's sobbing. what does Al-Baqi let you tell him?
options: everything made passes; only He remains, so we can make things lightly.
build it farther up the beach; strong enough, it can last for good.
that's why making things is pointless; the sea always wins anyway.
fork.reveal: Al-Baqi doesn't make things pointless. if He alone remains, the sandcastle can be loved, enjoyed, and let go.

original.note: Arabic: the Everlasting, the One who remains; from the traditional list of the Names.

trapdoor: what you thought: Allah simply lives a very long time.
what it means: He remains when everything perishes, and what is given to Him remains with Him.
what a scholar hears: 28:88 and 16:96 read beside the hadith of the sheep, 'all of it remains except its shoulder' (Tirmidhi 2470).
guess: the Everlasting, who remains when all else passes
the Patient, who waits before He answers you
the Keeper, who stores up what people own

chat.says: dadi gave her good dishes to the neighbors. kept ONE chipped cup. why am i the sad one
options: Sad is fair. But the hadith says the given part is what remains; she kept the rest.
Don't be sad. Stuff never matters, so none of her dishes ever meant anything.
Rescue a few. Keeping her things safe is how what she loves will remain.
chat.meaning: In the hadith, the given-away sheep remains and the kept shoulder doesn't. What is with Allah remains.
